info.bio: The Spinners es un grupo vocal estadounidense de rhythm and blues creado en 1954 en Ferndale, Michigan. El grupo tuvo una serie de exitosos sencillos y álbumes durante las décadas de los años sesenta y setenta, particularmente junto al productor Thom Bell.

scenes.desc: El imperio de Kenny Gamble y Leon Huff, distribuido por CBS: los O’Jays, los Intruders, Billy Paul y Harold Melvin & the Blue Notes con Teddy Pendergrass, sobre la banda de la casa MFSB (Norman Harris, Bobby Eli, Ronnie Baker, Earl Young), la más exitosa de los setenta; su «TSOP» fue la sintonía de Soul Train. Los O’Jays fueron el altavoz del comentario social de Gamble: «Back Stabbers» (1972), Ship Ahoy (1974) con su travesía en un barco negrero, «For the Love of Money» (que el éxito convirtió en música de centro comercial), Survival, Family Reunion. Después de 1976 desapareció el mensaje del soul, y con Gloria Gaynor y Donna Summer la frontera entre el disco, el funk y el soul se borró.

podcast.title: Zaire 74 Accommodations & Interaction (1974)
podcast.body: Ruth Pointer of The Pointer Sisters mentioned that the presence of The Spinners staying nearby helped alleviate boredom with the "out in the sticks" accommodations in Zaire. The documentary "Soul Power" features notable footage of Philippe Wynne sparring with Muhammad Ali and captures The Spinners' visually striking stage presence in "glittery white jackets" with "zaggedy white lightning bolt things" and "smooth moves" while performing "One of a Kind Love Affair." "Some of the best film footage of the spinners in the documentary Soul Power is a Philippe win sparring with Ali."

podcast.title: Shared Appearances on American Bandstand and Soul Train (1976-1977)
podcast.body: The Spinners were among several notable artists, including The Undisputed Truth, KC and the Sunshine Band, and Donna Summer, who appeared on both American Bandstand and Soul Train during 1976 and 1977. This demonstrated the capacity for both shows to coexist and feature popular musical talent. "the undispeed of truth is on both shows. Casey and the Sunshine Band, Donna Summer, the Spinners, there are more."

podcast.title: Move to Atlantic Records (Early 1970s)
podcast.body: Dissatisfied with their progress at Motown, The Spinners decided to leave for Atlantic Records, viewing it as a suitable label given its success with artists like Aretha Franklin. This move, combined with Philippe Wynne joining the group (replacing G.C. Cameron, who remained at Motown) and their collaboration with producer Thom Bell, enabled them to become "the perfect vehicle for that Philly sound," characterized by gorgeous falsetto, lush orchestration, and a smoothly polished sound. "So they left for Atlantic records because they were thinking, look, if Atlantic records is good enough for Arita Franklin, it's good enough for us."

podcast.title: Poor Treatment at Motown
podcast.body: The Spinners experienced unfavorable conditions at Motown, where they received significantly less attention compared to groups like The Temptations and The Four Tops and were even assigned duties as chauffeurs for other artists. "The spinners, they'd been done wrong by Motown, who gave a lot more attention to the temptations and to the four tops."

srcs.episode: Ep. 37 - Philly Soul and the Sound of the 70s

podcast.title: Tom Bell's Impact
podcast.body: Tom Bell played a transformative role in The Spinners' career after their departure from Motown, producing a string of hits at Atlantic Records that elevated them to stardom. "Tom Bell made them into stars."

srcs.episode: Ep. 37 - Philly Soul and the Sound of the 70s

podcast.title: Tom Bell's Wager
podcast.body: To persuade The Spinners to allow him to produce their next record, Tom Bell offered a wager: he would pay each member $1,000 if he failed to deliver a number one hit, but if successful, they would owe him a custom Cadillac. He achieved a number one hit with "I'll Be Around" but graciously forewent collecting the Cadillac, humorously noting he couldn't drive anyway. "If I do not get you a number one record, I will give each one of you $1,000. If I do get you a number one record, you owe me a custom Cadillac."
